ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: the road calls
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: A camp of travelers on the colony's land, and a colonist who has spent evenings at their fire and half wants to go with them when they leave. In the end, the camp goes, and they stay.

li.label: evenings at their fire
li.waiting: Next: {PAWN_nameDef} talks it over with someone at home.

plain.li: Spent the evening at the camp again. {NAME} told stories of the roads south until the fire was ash. I didn't want to come home.
The people at the camp have been everywhere. I've been here. I've started to notice the difference.
[night] Walked back from the camp under the stars and thought, I could just keep walking. I didn't. I thought it, though.
They pack everything they own onto their backs every few weeks. I counted my things tonight and wondered what I'd take.

warm.li: The travelers at the camp made me feel like an old friend. I keep going back for that, and for the singing.

blunt.li: The camp's people go where they like. I'm starting to envy that.

cheerful.li: Another evening at the camp! I've learned two songs and a card game and the names of four rivers.

gloomy.li: Everyone at the camp is going somewhere. I'm only going to the fields tomorrow, and the day after.

cold.li: The travelers carry everything they need and owe no one anything. I've been doing the sums on that.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has been spending evenings at the travelers' camp, listening to {NAME}'s stories of the road.
The camp's fire draws {PAWN_nameDef} most evenings now.

li.label: half packed
li.waiting: Next: the camp packs up and moves on, and {PAWN_nameDef} decides.

plain.li: Told {OTHER_nameDef} I'd been thinking about leaving with the camp. {OTHER_nameDef} didn't argue. {OTHER_nameDef} just went very still.
I've half packed a bag. It's under my bed. I look at it in the mornings.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me what I'd be looking for out there. I couldn't say. That probably means something.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said I'd be missed. Not to make me stay. Just so I'd know. I keep thinking about it.

blunt.li: Might go with the camp. Might not. Haven't decided.

cheerful.li: I could go anywhere! I won't, probably, but I could, and that feels wonderful.

gloomy.li: If I go, I lose everything here. If I stay, I lose whatever's out there. Either way I lose.

cold.li: I have listed what I would gain and lose by leaving. The lists are close in length.

chronicle.li: There's a half-packed bag under {PAWN_nameDef}'s bed, for when the camp moves on.

plain.li: The camp went this morning. I walked with them as far as the boundary stone, and then I came home. I unpacked the bag tonight.
{NAME} shook my hand at the edge of our land and said the road would keep. It will. So will I.
I stayed. I hung the bag back on its hook and slept in my own bed, and slept well.

warm.li: I stayed, and {OTHER_nameDef} had saved my seat at supper. That's what I'd have been leaving.

blunt.li: The camp's gone. I'm still here. Decided.

cheerful.li: I stayed. I'll have stories of the road anyway, second-hand, which is the safest kind.

gloomy.li: They've gone, and I watched them go. I'll always wonder. I'll wonder here, though.

cold.li: The camp has departed. I remain. On reflection, the colony's claims on me were the stronger.

chronicle.li: When the camp moved on, {PAWN_nameDef} walked them to the boundary stone and came home.
"The road will keep," the travelers told {PAWN_nameDef} when they left. {PAWN_nameDef} came home.

li.label: the walk to the edge of the land

plain.li: [campfight] The travelers turned on us. All those evenings at their fire, and they turned on us. I don't know what I'd have become out there with them.
[timeout] The camp's still here and so am I, and the bag is still under my bed. Some questions don't get answered.
I stopped going to the camp's fire. Whatever was calling me has stopped.

gloomy.li: [campfight] I trusted them. I was going to go with them. I feel like a fool.

fizzleChronicle.li: [campfight] The camp turned on the colony, and {PAWN_nameDef} stopped thinking about the road.
{PAWN_nameDef} stopped going to the camp's fire.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} could have left with the travelers that season, and stayed with us instead. I hope it was worth it to {OTHER_objective}.
{OTHER_nameDef} used to talk about the road. I'll walk some of it for {OTHER_objective} one day.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} chose to stay. The choice is final now, in more ways than one.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: the weight of office
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Newly seated on the council, a colonist isn't sure they can carry it. Advice from someone who has sat there, some doubtful days, a hard call, and growing into it, unless the seat is lost first.

plain.li: I'm {NAME} now. Everyone keeps congratulating me. I keep smiling and thinking, they'll find out.
The first morning as {NAME}. Three people asked me things I didn't know, and I said I'd look into it. I said that three times.
I wanted this seat. I didn't think about what it would feel like to have it.

warm.li: They chose me as {NAME}. I want to do right by them. I'm afraid of letting them down.

blunt.li: I'm {NAME}. Fine. I'll learn the job.

cheerful.li: I'm {NAME}! I have no idea what I'm doing, and it's wonderful and terrifying.

gloomy.li: Made {NAME}. Everyone will be watching for the first mistake. There'll be one soon.

cold.li: Made {NAME}. I've written down what the office owes, and to whom. It's a long page. I'll get through it.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, newly made {NAME}, isn't yet sure {PAWN_pronoun} can carry the office.
Three people came to {PAWN_nameDef} on {PAWN_possessive} first morning as {NAME}, and {PAWN_nameDef} promised all three to look into it.

li.label: doubtful days
li.waiting: Next: some steady days, or {PAWN_nameDef}'s faith in the council holding.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me nobody is ready for a seat on the council, and everyone pretends. It helped more than it should have.
Took {OTHER_nameDef}'s advice and asked for help with the things I don't know. Nobody laughed. Two people looked relieved.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat with me half the night going over the office. I'll pass that on to whoever sits here next.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} says everyone's bad at it at first. Good. I'm right on schedule.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} gave me some good advice, and I've written it all down! Somewhere.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} tried to make me feel better. It worked until morning.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s advice was practical. I have adopted most of it.

chronicle.li: "Nobody is ready for a seat on the council," {OTHER_nameDef} told {PAWN_nameDef}. "Everyone pretends."

li.label: a hard call
li.waiting: Next: a few more days in the seat.

plain.li: Had to make a call today that somebody won't like. Made it anyway. Slept badly. Got up and did the next thing.
Someone came to me as {NAME} today, angry, and I handled it. I'm not sure how. I did.

warm.li: I had to say no to someone I care about today, as {NAME}. I explained why. I think they understood.

blunt.li: Made a hard call. Would make it again.

cheerful.li: Survived my first real decision as {NAME}! Not a single bowl was thrown.

gloomy.li: I made the call. I'll find out in a week whether it was the wrong one.

cold.li: A difficult decision was required of me, and I made it. That is what the office is for.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} made a hard call as {NAME}, and stood by it.

plain.li: Someone called me {NAME} today and I answered without thinking. The seat fits now.
I'm still not sure I'm good at this. I'm sure I'm better at it than I was, and that's enough to go on.
A newcomer asked me how I learned to be {NAME}. I told them what {OTHER_nameDef} told me.

warm.li: I've grown into the office. I hope I've grown into the kind of {NAME} people can come to.

blunt.li: I'm {NAME}. I'm good at it now. Next question.

cheerful.li: I'm a real {NAME} now, not a pretend one. Most days, anyway.

gloomy.li: I've got the hang of it. That means the hard part is just beginning, I expect.

cold.li: I have become competent in the office. Competence is not glamorous, but it is what was asked for.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has grown into the office of {NAME}.
{PAWN_nameDef} answers to "{NAME}" now without looking round to see who's meant.

plain.li: [officegone] I'm not {NAME} any more. I was only just learning how.
[timeout] I hold the office still. I'm just not sure I'll ever feel I deserve it.
Whatever I hoped to become in that seat, I haven't, not yet.

blunt.li: [officegone] Lost the seat. Fine. Their loss.

gloomy.li: [officegone] They took the seat away before I'd learned to sit in it. I knew they would.

warm.li: [officegone] Someone else has the office now. I'll help them the way {OTHER_nameDef} helped me.

fizzleChronicle.li: [officegone] {PAWN_nameDef} lost the seat of {NAME} before {PAWN_pronoun} had grown into it.
{PAWN_nameDef} never quite felt at home in the office of {NAME}.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was still learning to carry the office when {OTHER_pronoun} died, and learning fast.
{OTHER_nameDef} used to say nobody is ready for a seat on the council. {OTHER_nameDef} was more ready than {OTHER_pronoun} knew.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died in office. The office continues. That is what offices are for.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: word from far away
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Hard times out in the world (a plague, a famine, a war, a flood), and family of theirs out there in it. Worry shared with someone at home, the long wait, and word at last, or the worst news.

li.label: news on the wind
li.waiting: Next: {PAWN_nameDef} shares the worry with someone.

plain.li: The traders all say the same thing this season, "{NAME}", and the place they say it about is where {LOST} lives. I can't stop thinking about it.
{LOST} is out there among {FACTION}, in the middle of all that. I don't even know if {LOST} has heard my name in years.
[night] Lay awake counting the days it would take to reach {LOST}. Too many. Far too many.

warm.li: I hope someone out there is looking after {LOST}. I'd give a lot to be the one doing it.

blunt.li: Bad news from out there, and {LOST} in it. Nothing I can do. I hate that.

cheerful.li: {LOST} always lands on both feet. Always has. I'm sure it'll be the same this time.

gloomy.li: The traders say "{NAME}" and won't meet my eye. {LOST} is out there in it. I already know how this ends.

cold.li: The trouble out there has reached {FACTION}, and {LOST} is among them. I have no means of learning more.

chronicle.li: The traders' news this season is "{NAME}", and {PAWN_nameDef} has family out in it: {LOST}, among {FACTION}.
{PAWN_nameDef} has family far away, {LOST}, and the news from the road is bad.

li.label: waiting for word
li.waiting: Next: the hard times out there end, or word comes some other way.

plain.li: Told {OTHER_nameDef} about {LOST} last night, all of it. Saying it out loud changed nothing, and still I slept better.
I've asked every trader and traveler about {FACTION}. Not one of them knows anything about one person among so many.
Wrote a letter to {LOST}. No idea how it'll get there. The next trader took it, and a coin for luck.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat up with me and let me talk about {LOST}. I'm lucky in my friends here, even if I'm unlucky in where my family is.

cheerful.li: No news is good news, everybody says. I'm choosing to believe everybody.

gloomy.li: Every day without word is another day to imagine the worst. I'm good at imagining.

cold.li: I have done what I can: a letter sent, travelers questioned. The rest is waiting.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} waits for word of {LOST}, asking every traveler who passes.

plain.li: The hard times out there have passed, and word came down the road: {LOST} came through it. Thinner, older, alive. I sat down in the dirt and laughed.
{LOST} is alive. That's all the message said, and it's all I needed it to say.
Word came back with the letter I sent: {LOST} read it. {LOST} is well. {LOST} sends love, and a recipe I'd forgotten.

warm.li: {LOST} is safe, and someone out there among {FACTION} was kind to {LOST} when it mattered. I'd like to thank them.

blunt.li: {LOST}'s alive. Good. I can sleep now.

cheerful.li: {LOST} made it! Of course {LOST} did. I told everyone {LOST} would.

gloomy.li: {LOST} lived through it. I don't know what to do with good news. I'll learn.

cold.li: {LOST} survived. I'd been holding my breath for weeks without noticing.

chronicle.li: Word reached {PAWN_nameDef} at last. {LOST} came through it alive.
{PAWN_nameDef} has heard that {LOST}, far away among {FACTION}, is safe.

plain.li: [kindead] Word came. {LOST} didn't come through it. I was here, far away, and never even knew until it was over.
[kindead] {LOST} is dead. Somewhere among {FACTION} there's a grave I'll never see.
[timeout] No word, still. I've stopped asking the traders. I haven't stopped hoping.
I don't know what became of {LOST}. Perhaps I never will.

warm.li: [kindead] {LOST} is gone. I hope someone held {LOST}'s hand at the end. I hope it wasn't lonely.

blunt.li: [kindead] {LOST}'s dead. Don't talk to me today.

gloomy.li: [kindead] I knew. From the first day the traders said it, I knew.

cold.li: [kindead] {LOST} did not survive. There was nothing I could have done from here. That is no comfort.

fizzleChronicle.li: [kindead] {LOST}, family of {PAWN_nameDef}'s far away among {FACTION}, did not live through the hard times.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} spent {OTHER_possessive} last weeks worrying about family far away. I hope word of {OTHER_objective} reaches them one day.
{OTHER_nameDef} wrote a letter to someone out there. I'll write the next one.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died waiting for word from far away. Someone should send word back.
